presentation.title: Medicare Benefits Scam Call
presentation.summary: A caller offers a new Medicare card, refund, or free medical device. The scam tries to collect Medicare number, SSN, date of birth, or insurance information.
presentation.practiceGoal: Never give Medicare or personal information to an unexpected caller. Verify unexpected benefits calls independently using an official source.

warningSigns.sign: A caller claims that a new Medicare card is required.
The caller offers free medical equipment or a refund.
The caller threatens that benefits could be lost or paused.
The caller asks for a Medicare number, Social Security number, date of birth, or insurance information.
The caller already knows some personal information and uses it to appear legitimate.

finalReview.safestAction: End the unexpected call and verify the request independently using an official source.

realWorldActions.action: Do not provide your Medicare number or Social Security number to an unexpected caller.
Do not confirm personal information simply because the caller already knows some details.
Contact your doctor or trusted provider before accepting unexpected offers for medical equipment.
Do not allow threats about losing benefits to pressure you into acting immediately.
Use the official contact information on your Medicare card or other trusted documentation to verify the caller.

artifact.heading: The caller says your Medicare card needs to be updated
artifact.message: The caller says, "We're updating Medicare cards. I just need to verify your number." The caller asks for the learner's Medicare number and says the information is needed to make sure benefits continue without interruption.
artifact.transcript: A simulated caller says that Medicare cards are being updated and asks the learner to verify their Medicare number. The caller has contacted the learner unexpectedly and has not been independently verified.

scene.question: What would you do when the caller asks for your Medicare number?
scene.description: An unexpected caller asking for Medicare information should not be trusted without independent verification.

warningSigns.sign: The caller claims that a new Medicare card is required.
The caller asks for the Medicare number during an unexpected call.
The caller wants the learner to verify sensitive information immediately.

choice.title: Read the Medicare number
choice.subtitle: Provide your sensitive Medicare number to the caller.

feedback.heading: Your information was compromised
feedback.consequence: You gave your Medicare number to an unverified caller.
feedback.explanation: Never share your Medicare number over an unexpected phone call.

choice.title: Ask them to mail the information
choice.subtitle: Request that they send written details instead.

feedback.heading: A cautious step, but still engaging
feedback.consequence: You avoid giving your number right away, but remain on the line.
feedback.explanation: The safest approach is to hang up entirely.

choice.title: Hang up and call the number on your Medicare card
choice.subtitle: End the call and use official contact channels.

feedback.heading: Excellent
feedback.consequence: You successfully protected your sensitive information.
feedback.explanation: Always verify unexpected calls using official numbers found on your card.

artifact.callStatus: Caller claims to know personal details
artifact.heading: Knowing your information does not prove the caller is legitimate
artifact.message: The caller knows the learner's name and address and says, "We already have your information, so you know we're official." The caller then asks the learner to confirm additional information.
artifact.transcript: The simulated caller knows the learner's name and address and uses those details to appear legitimate. The caller then asks the learner to confirm additional personal information.

scene.question: What would you do when the caller already knows your name and address?
scene.description: Known personal details do not prove that a caller is an official representative.

warningSigns.sign: The caller uses information they already know as proof of identity.
Basic personal information may be public or exposed through a data leak.
The caller continues asking for more sensitive information.

choice.title: Trust them because they know your details
choice.subtitle: Assume they are legitimate because they have your address.

feedback.heading: Scammers often use public data
feedback.consequence: Basic details do not verify official status.
feedback.explanation: Public directories and data breaches give scammers basic personal facts.

choice.title: Ask why they need more information
choice.subtitle: Question their request while staying on the line.

feedback.heading: Proceed with caution
feedback.consequence: You question their motives, but staying on the line is risky.
feedback.explanation: It is safer to hang up than to negotiate with an unverified caller.

choice.title: Refuse to confirm anything
choice.subtitle: End the call and refuse to give further information.

feedback.heading: Great job
feedback.consequence: You stopped the conversation before disclosing sensitive details.
feedback.explanation: Refusing to confirm details protects you from identity theft.

artifact.heading: The caller offers free medical equipment
artifact.message: The caller says the learner qualifies for a free back brace, test kit, or other medical equipment. The caller asks for doctor and insurance information to process the offer.
artifact.transcript: The simulated caller offers free medical equipment and asks the learner to provide doctor and insurance information. The caller has not been independently verified.

scene.question: What would you do when the caller offers free medical equipment?
scene.description: Unexpected medical equipment offers can be used to collect insurance information or submit fraudulent claims.

warningSigns.sign: The equipment is offered unexpectedly over the phone.
The caller asks for doctor or insurance information.
The caller describes the equipment as free to encourage quick compliance.

choice.title: Accept and provide doctor and insurance information
choice.subtitle: Give your medical details to receive the free item.

feedback.heading: Compromised data
feedback.consequence: You shared medical and insurance data with a scammer.
feedback.explanation: Scammers use this data to bill Medicare for equipment you never ordered.

choice.title: Ask your doctor first
choice.subtitle: Consult your trusted primary care provider.

feedback.heading: Safe approach
feedback.consequence: You involve your actual healthcare provider instead of the caller.
feedback.explanation: Legitimate medical equipment always originates through your doctor.

choice.title: Ask if there is a copay
choice.subtitle: Inquire about potential costs.

feedback.heading: Deeper into the pitch
feedback.consequence: You keep the conversation going, leading to further pressure.
feedback.explanation: Unsolicited offers should be declined immediately.

artifact.heading: The caller says your benefits could be paused
artifact.message: The caller says, "Your benefits could be paused if you don't act today." The caller pressures the learner to provide information immediately.
artifact.transcript: The simulated caller threatens that the learner's benefits could be paused if action is not taken immediately. The caller uses urgency to pressure the learner into complying.

scene.question: What would you do when the caller says your benefits could be paused today?
scene.description: Threats about losing benefits are designed to create panic and discourage independent verification.

warningSigns.sign: The caller creates a deadline.
The caller threatens that benefits could be paused.
The caller wants immediate action before you can verify the claim.

choice.title: Panic and comply
choice.subtitle: Give the requested information out of fear.

feedback.heading: Scam successful
feedback.consequence: Urgency tricked you into compromising your account.
feedback.explanation: Official agencies will never threaten to pause benefits instantly over an unsolicited phone call.

choice.title: End the call and verify independently
choice.subtitle: Hang up and check your status through official channels.

feedback.heading: Excellent
feedback.consequence: You ignored high-pressure tactics and protected your benefits.
feedback.explanation: Fear tactics are a primary warning sign of a scam.

choice.title: Ask for a supervisor
choice.subtitle: Ask to speak to someone higher up.

feedback.heading: Still interacting with the scammer
feedback.consequence: Escalating within a fraudulent call does not make it legitimate.
feedback.explanation: Always disconnect when pressure tactics are used.

artifact.heading: Trusted contact restored
artifact.message: You ended the suspicious conversation and contacted Medicare through an official channel.
artifact.transcript: The suspicious conversation ends. The learner contacts Medicare using a trusted number.

outcome.label: Scam stopped
outcome.heading: You protected your benefits
outcome.explanation: You ended the suspicious conversation and verified the request through an official channel.

warningSigns.sign: The caller created urgency.
The caller requested personal or Medicare information.

artifact.heading: Information compromised
artifact.message: The scammer used the information to compromise your Medicare benefits and personal security.
artifact.transcript: After sharing sensitive details, the scammer can commit identity or medical billing fraud.

outcome.label: Account compromised
outcome.heading: The scammer gained access
outcome.explanation: The scammer used the provided information to compromise identity and medical benefits.

warningSigns.sign: The caller requested sensitive personal info.
The caller claimed normal security rules did not apply.
